card.summary: The AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act of 2025 directs the Department of Transportation to issue a rule requiring new passenger vehicles manufactured or imported into the United States to include standard equipment capable of receiving and playing AM broadcast signals or digital audio AM signals easily accessible to drivers. Before the final rule takes effect, manufacturers producing vehicles without AM equipment must provide clear labeling and may not charge separate fees for AM access. The bill also preempts state and local laws regarding AM access in motor vehicles, sets enforcement mechanisms and penalties, mandates a Government Accountability Office study on public emergency alerts, requires periodic reports, and establishes an expiration date for the rule and authority.

summary: The S. 315 bill, titled the AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act of 2025, requires the Department of Transportation to issue a rule mandating that all new passenger motor vehicles manufactured or imported for sale in the United States include AM radio capabilities as standard equipment. Before the new rule takes effect, manufacturers who omit AM radio must clearly label vehicles stating the lack of AM access and cannot charge extra fees for it. The legislation also blocks state and local governments from creating their own rules regarding AM radio access in vehicles, establishes civil penalties for rule violations, requires the Government Accountability Office to study public emergency alert systems, and sunsets the rule and enforcement authority 10 years after enactment.

affected_groups.effect: Must include AM radio or digital audio AM equipment as standard, accessible equipment in new passenger motor vehicles after a set effective date, apply warning labels on interim vehicles without AM radio, and face potential civil penalties for noncompliance.
Will have guaranteed access to standard AM radio capabilities in new passenger motor vehicles without extra charges, and will receive warning labels if interim vehicles lack AM functionality.
Prohibited from establishing or continuing any laws, regulations, or requirements related to AM radio access in passenger motor vehicles.

key_provisions: Requires the Department of Transportation, in consultation with FEMA and the FCC, to issue a rule within one year requiring AM radio or digital audio AM stations as standard equipment in new passenger vehicles.
Sets compliance timelines generally between two and three years after the rule is issued, with at least four years for smaller manufacturers who produced 40,000 or fewer vehicles in 2022.
Mandates interim labeling requirements for vehicles produced between enactment and the final rule's effective date if they lack AM radio, prohibiting any extra fees for AM access during this period.
Preempts state and local laws, regulations, or requirements regarding access to AM broadcast stations in passenger motor vehicles.
Enforces the rule through civil penalties assessed by the federal government and civil actions brought by the Attorney General to enjoin violations.
Requires the Government Accountability Office to conduct a comprehensive study and report on public emergency alerts, warning systems, and the specific role of AM broadcast stations in vehicles.
Mandates periodic five-year reviews and reports by the Secretary of Transportation, and sets a 10-year sunset on the rule and the Secretary's authority to enforce it.
missing_information: Exact dollar amounts for civil penalties are not specified within the text, as they reference general statutory penalty frameworks.
The specific baseline base prices of vehicles are not defined.
